Syringomyelia (cavitation of the spinal cord).

In syringomyelia, the central canal cavitation disrupts the decussating spinothalamic fibers (pain and temperature) because they cross in the anterior white commissure near the center of the spinal cord. Proprioception and fine touch (dorsal columns) are spared as they ascend ipsilaterally without crossing.
The cervical enlargement (C5-T1) is the most common site for syringomyelia because it is the widest part of the spinal cord with a high concentration of crossing spinothalamic fibers.
